compiled_state.title: pre-commit-compliance-verifier blocks sub-agent worktree commits in ci-pr mode
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`pre-commit-compliance-verifier.sh` requires artifacts (`test.result`, `format.result`, `lint.result`, `classifier-dispatch.result`, `reviewer-record.result`) to exist before allowing a commit. The hook does NOT respect `dso.workflow=ci-pr` (review enforcement deferred to CI). This blocks worktree-isolated sub-agents from committing test files cleanly during sprint Phase C dispatch, since they would need to run the full local commit workflow (commit-step.sh + review-workflow.sh) to produce those artifacts — defeating the point of ci-pr mode.

## Reproduction

Sprint epic f691-681e-0db9-4260, Phase C batch 3 (2026-05-19):
1. Sprint orchestrator in session worktree with `.sprint-active` marker.
2. Project config: `dso.workflow=ci-pr` (review enforcement = CI, not local).
3. Dispatched 4 RED-test-writer sub-agents in parallel with `isolation: "worktree"`.
4. Two sub-agents (S2.T1, S4.T1) completed their internal commit workflow successfully — commits landed on session via the harvest mechanism.
5. Two sub-agents (S5.T1=4311-b135-85d4-4fa8, S6.T1=406b-9d59-acc6-45c0) wrote tests but did NOT commit; their changes appeared uncommitted in the orchestrator's session worktree.
6. Attempting to commit those changes via a fresh story worktree was blocked:
   ```
   ERROR: pre-commit-compliance-verifier: required artifact 'classifier-dispatch.result' not found — run commit-step before committing
   ERROR: pre-commit-compliance-verifier: required artifact 'reviewer-record.result' not found — run commit-step before committing
   ERROR: pre-commit-compliance-verifier: required artifact 'format.result' not found — run commit-step before committing
   ERROR: pre-commit-compliance-verifier: required artifact 'lint.result' not found — run commit-step before committing
   ```

## Expected behavior

When `dso.workflow=ci-pr` is set, the compliance verifier should auto-skip for sub-agent worktree commits (where the artifacts dir is empty / freshly-created), because the entire point of ci-pr mode is to defer review to GitHub-side CI (via the new review-sub-pr.yml + ci.yml/llm-review). Requiring local artifacts contradicts the ci-pr design intent.

The orchestrator's primary worktree (with sprint-active marker) can still enforce — the constraint should apply there, not in dispatched sub-agent worktrees.

## Current behavior

The hook checks `hooks.compliance_verifier.enabled` boolean only. It does NOT check `dso.workflow=ci-pr`. Result: when compliance_verifier is enabled, EVERY worktree (orchestrator + sub-agent) must produce the 5 artifacts, regardless of workflow mode.

## Suggested fix

Add an early-exit branch in `pre-commit-compliance-verifier.sh` (around line 26, before the artifacts-dir check):

```bash
# Skip compliance verifier in ci-pr mode for non-orchestrator worktrees.
# When dso.workflow=ci-pr, review enforcement is the CI's responsibility
# (review-sub-pr.yml + ci.yml/llm-review). Sub-agent worktrees committing
# RED tests or implementation work should not be required to also run the
# local commit-step pipeline that produces these artifacts.
_workflow=$(grep -m1 '^dso\.workflow=' "$_REPO_ROOT/.claude/dso-config.conf" 2>/dev/null | cut -d= -f2-)
if [[ "$_workflow" == "ci-pr" ]]; then
    # In ci-pr mode, only the primary checkout enforces; sub-agent worktrees skip.
    _is_primary_checkout=$(test -d "$_REPO_ROOT/.git" && echo "yes" || echo "no")
    if [[ "$_is_primary_checkout" == "no" ]]; then
        # Sub-agent worktree: skip compliance verifier — CI will enforce on PR.
        exit 0
    fi
fi
```

Alternative: a config flag `hooks.compliance_verifier.skip_in_worktrees=true` that operators can set explicitly.

## Workaround used during sprint Phase C batch 3

For S5.T1 + S6.T1, the recovery patch was saved at `/tmp/sprint-f691-batch3-s5t1-s6t1-RECOVERY.patch` (38K, 217 + 633 lines of RED test additions). The tasks were reverted to `open` status with checkpoint comments pointing to the recovery patch. Tickets 4311-b135-85d4-4fa8 (S5.T1) and 406b-9d59-acc6-45c0 (S6.T1) are blocked pending either: (a) the compliance verifier fix above, OR (b) re-dispatch of the sub-agents with an explicit override mechanism, OR (c) direct merge via `git merge --no-ff worktree-branch --no-edit` (the pattern that worked for batches 1 and 2 where sub-agents successfully completed their commits).

Note that the `commit-override.sh` script exists but requires interactive invocation; it's not callable from an orchestrator session.

## Impact

Blocks Phase C parallel dispatch when dso.workflow=ci-pr. Sub-agents that succeed at committing (via internal pipeline) work; sub-agents that fail silently leave uncommitted changes that the orchestrator cannot route through normal commit. The asymmetry between S2.T1/S4.T1 (success) and S5.T1/S6.T1 (silent commit failure) needs investigation: why do some sub-agents complete the pipeline and others don't? Possibly related to commit-step.sh exit handling on lint/format failures.

## Related

- Epic f691-681e (sprint that surfaced this)
- CLAUDE.md rule 9 (raw git commit prohibition)
- CLAUDE.md rule 24 (sprint-active merge-only enforcement)
- plugins/dso/docs/workflows/COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md (the workflow that produces the required artifacts)

comments.body: Fixed: PR #236 merged to main as 52991360fd. The compliance-verifier hook now auto-skips when (dso.workflow=ci-pr) AND running in a git worktree AND DSO_COMPLIANCE_VERIFIER_ENABLED is unset. Primary checkout still enforces. Existing 15-test hook test suite passes unchanged. Bonus: rolled in the .test-index RED marker fixes (cycle-ledger-migration, scan-red-markers) + S5.T1/S6.T1 recovery patch + cafb change-detector regression fix from S1.T5.
